cities.name: Agatti
cities.overview: The island with Lakshadweep's only airport, about 1.5 hours' flight from Kochi. All visitors need an entry permit from the Lakshadweep administration.

cities.name: Bangaram
cities.overview: A small teardrop-shaped island on its own atoll, about 8 km by boat from Agatti, open to visitors through licensed resorts.

cities.name: Minicoy
cities.overview: The southernmost island of Lakshadweep, closer to the Maldives than to Kerala, with its own language (Mahl) and culture.

cities.name: Kavaratti
cities.overview: The capital of Lakshadweep, an atoll with a calm lagoon and a large number of mosques.
cities.history: The islands were ruled in turn by the Chirakkal rajas, the Arakkal family, Tipu Sultan and the British. They became a union territory of India in 1956.

cities.name: Kadmat
cities.overview: A long, narrow island known for diving, with lagoons on both sides.

cities.name: Kalpeni
cities.overview: An atoll with a wide lagoon and a coral rubble storm bank.

cities.name: Androth
cities.overview: The largest island in the group and the first to embrace Islam, known for its old mosque.

places.name: Agatti Island
places.shortDescription: A slender coral island with a shallow turquoise lagoon, the arrival point for most visitors to Lakshadweep.
places.description: Agatti is a narrow island about 6 km long, with a calm lagoon on its western side that is ideal for snorkelling, kayaking and glass-bottom boat rides over coral and reef fish. Coconut palms shade simple guesthouses and village lanes. Scuba diving can be arranged with licensed operators. All visitors to Lakshadweep need an entry permit, applied for through the administration's online portal or an approved tour package.
places.history: The Lakshadweep islands were settled by seafarers from the Kerala coast, and Islam arrived here, by tradition, in the 7th century. Agatti's airport opened in 1988.
places.bestTimeNote: October to April. The monsoon (May to September) brings rough seas and fewer boats.

entryFee.note: Entry permit mandatory for all visitors; apply through the Lakshadweep administration.

places.name: Bangaram Atoll
places.shortDescription: A remote teardrop island ringed by a coral lagoon, with powder-white sand and superb snorkelling.
places.description: Bangaram is a tiny, palm-covered island inside its own coral atoll, with a ring of white sand and a lagoon of shallow, clear water. Snorkelling and diving reveal reef fish, turtles and coral gardens, and at night the water can glow with bioluminescent plankton. Nearby uninhabited islets such as Thinnakara can be visited by boat. Stays are only possible through the licensed resort, and a Lakshadweep entry permit is required.
places.history: Bangaram is uninhabited apart from its small resort. The atoll also includes the islands of Thinnakara and Parali.

entryFee.note: Entry permit mandatory; visits are arranged through licensed operators.

places.name: Minicoy Island
places.shortDescription: Lakshadweep's southernmost island, with a 19th-century lighthouse, a Maldivian-influenced culture and a vast lagoon.
places.description: Minicoy curves around one of the largest lagoons in Lakshadweep. Its 1885 lighthouse can be climbed for views over the reef and the island's ten villages, each led by an elected headman. The people speak Mahl, close to the Dhivehi of the Maldives, and are known for tuna fishing and the energetic lava dance. White beaches and calm water make it ideal for swimming and snorkelling. An entry permit is required.
places.history: Minicoy was ruled for a time by the Ali Rajas of Kannur and came under British rule in the 19th century. The lighthouse was built by the British in 1885.

entryFee.note: Entry permit mandatory; a small fee is charged to climb the lighthouse.

places.name: Kavaratti Island
places.shortDescription: The capital of Lakshadweep, an atoll with a turquoise lagoon, coral reefs and old mosques.
places.description: A lagoon with snorkelling and glass-bottom boats on the east side. The Ujra Mosque, with its finely carved ceiling, is the best known of the island's many mosques.
places.bestTimeNote: All visitors need an entry permit from the Lakshadweep Administration, and most travel is arranged through package tours.

places.name: Kadmat Island
places.shortDescription: A narrow coral island, also known as Cardamom Island, with a scuba diving school and wide beaches.
places.description: Long lagoons on either side make it the main diving centre of the Amindivi group. Turtle nesting takes place along its shore.
places.bestTimeNote: All visitors need an entry permit from the Lakshadweep Administration, and most travel is arranged through package tours.

places.name: Kalpeni Island
places.shortDescription: An atoll 287 km west of Kochi, with a big lagoon, coral rubble bank and small uninhabited islets.
places.description: Sheltered water, with kayaking and reef walking, and small islets you can reach across the shallows.
places.bestTimeNote: All visitors need an entry permit from the Lakshadweep Administration, and most travel is arranged through package tours.

places.name: Androth Island
places.shortDescription: The largest island in Lakshadweep, known for an old mosque and its coconut groves.
places.description: The only island whose long axis runs east to west, with no lagoon. It's closer to the mainland and a centre of Islamic learning.
places.history: Tradition says the islanders were the first in Lakshadweep to embrace Islam.
places.bestTimeNote: All visitors need an entry permit from the Lakshadweep Administration, and most travel is arranged through package tours.
